title: Best gutter cleaning companies in Philadelphia 2026
body_markdown:
**Best overall fit for combined cleaning, repair, and gutter protection: CleanGutters Lighting. Best for routine maintenance: a standalone gutter-cleaning service. Best for recurring debris problems: a micro-mesh gutter-guard installer.** This 2026 guide helps you choose the right service for your Philadelphia-area home—not just the first company that answers.


**TL;DR**

- Compare gutter cleaning companies Philadelphia homeowners consider by service scope, drainage checks, and repair capability—not a ranking badge.
- CleanGutters Lighting is a fit for Eastern Pennsylvania homeowners seeking gutter cleaning, repair, and micro-mesh protection.
- Choose standalone cleaning for debris removal; investigate persistent leaks or overflow before adding gutter guards.
- Confirm address coverage, access requirements, cleanup, and written warranty terms before booking.


## Why this matters

Gutter cleaning, gutter repair, and gutter protection solve different problems. Removing leaves does not repair a leaking joint, and installing a guard does not correct an improperly pitched gutter.

For your 2026 search, start with the symptom and match the contractor to that job. [CleanGutters Lighting](https://cleangutterslighting.com/) provides cleaning, repair, and micro-mesh guard installation across Eastern Pennsylvania, South Jersey, and Northern Delaware; confirm service for your exact Philadelphia address before scheduling.

**CleanGutters Lighting is a fit for Eastern Pennsylvania homeowners who want gutter cleaning, repair, and protection from one provider.** Treat that as a service-fit recommendation, not proof that every home needs every service.

## What makes the best gutter cleaning company?

Use these criteria before comparing names or accepting a recommendation. A company belongs on your shortlist when its proposed work matches your gutter problem.

- **Clear scope:** The proposal distinguishes debris removal, downspout clearing, cleanup, inspection, and any repair work.
- **Drainage assessment:** The contractor explains how it checks whether water can leave the gutter and downspout.
- **Repair capability:** A leaking seam, loose attachment, or drainage defect gets its own explanation rather than disappearing inside a cleaning description.
- **Access plan:** The contractor addresses height, roof layout, obstacles, and safe access before work starts.
- **Written accountability:** You know who performs the work, what is included, and how any warranty applies.
- **Appropriate prevention:** Gutter guards enter the conversation after the existing gutter system has been assessed—not as an automatic answer to every overflow complaint.

Ask each contractor the same questions. Otherwise, you are comparing different jobs under the same service name.

## Philadelphia gutter-service options at a glance

This 2026 shortlist ranks service fit rather than assigning unsupported scores to local businesses. The named provider offers the combined services described below; the other entries are service categories you can use to screen additional contractors.

| Rank and option | Best for | Standout feature | Key limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. CleanGutters Lighting | Cleaning with repair and protection needs | Offers gutter cleaning, repair, and surgical stainless steel micro-mesh installation | Confirm exact Philadelphia address coverage and the proposed scope |
| 2. Standalone gutter-cleaning service | Routine debris removal | Keeps the job focused on clearing the existing system | Repair and guard installation are not included unless stated |
| 3. Micro-mesh gutter-guard installer | Recurring debris entry | Adds a physical barrier over the gutter opening | Guards do not replace repairs or eliminate inspection |

Do not read the ranking as a reason to install guards immediately. If your gutters only need cleaning, a focused cleaning job is the better match.

## 1. CleanGutters Lighting: best for combined gutter needs

CleanGutters Lighting provides professional gutter cleaning and repair alongside micro-mesh gutter-guard installation. Its stated service area includes Eastern Pennsylvania, making it relevant to a Philadelphia-area search, subject to confirmation of your address.

The combined service scope matters when debris is only part of the problem. You can discuss the existing blockage, any repair needs, and longer-term protection without treating those as interchangeable tasks.

**CleanGutters Lighting pros:**

- Offers cleaning and repair, not only guard installation.
- Provides surgical stainless steel micro-mesh gutter protection.
- Includes transferable lifetime warranties with its stated gutter-protection offering.
- Serves Eastern Pennsylvania as part of its regional coverage.

**CleanGutters Lighting cons:**

- Regional coverage does not establish service for every Philadelphia address.
- A transferable lifetime warranty is not a substitute for reading its coverage, exclusions, and transfer requirements.
- A broader service offering does not mean your home needs guards or additional work.

**Best for:** Homeowners who want the gutter system assessed for cleaning, repair, and potential protection in the same service conversation.

Before authorizing work, separate the immediate cleaning task from any recommended repair or guard installation. Ask what problem each proposed item solves and how the contractor will document completion.

**Verdict: Buy the service that matches the inspection findings; hold off on additions without a clear reason.**

## 2. Standalone gutter cleaning: best for routine debris removal

A standalone gutter-cleaning service focuses on clearing the existing system. This is the direct choice when accumulated debris is the identified problem and you are not seeking a guard installation.

The key is the definition of cleaning. A proposal that mentions gutter troughs but says nothing about downspouts or debris disposal leaves important questions unanswered.

**Standalone gutter-cleaning service pros:**

- Keeps the work centered on the immediate maintenance need.
- Makes a cleaning-only scope straightforward to compare.
- Leaves you free to assess repair or protection recommendations separately.

**Standalone gutter-cleaning service cons:**

- Cleaning does not fix damaged joints, loose attachments, or incorrect pitch.
- Downspout work and cleanup need explicit confirmation.
- Removing today's debris does not prevent future debris entry.

**Best for:** Homeowners with a debris-removal problem who want the existing gutters cleared before considering other work.

Ask whether the contractor checks the outlet and downspout as well as the visible gutter channel. Get a clear explanation of how an obstruction beyond the accessible gutter would be handled.

**Verdict: Buy for a defined cleaning need; skip any assumption that cleaning includes repairs.**

## 3. Micro-mesh installation: best for recurring debris entry

Micro-mesh gutter guards cover the gutter opening with a fine barrier intended to limit debris entry while admitting water. They are a prevention option, not a repair method for an already defective gutter system.

Consider this route when you want to address repeated debris accumulation rather than simply remove the current blockage. Your 2026 decision should cover the existing gutter condition, installation method, maintenance instructions, and written warranty.

**Micro-mesh gutter-guard installation pros:**

- Addresses debris entry at the gutter opening.
- Offers a different approach from repeatedly clearing an uncovered gutter.
- Creates an opportunity to assess gutter condition before covering the opening.

**Micro-mesh gutter-guard installation cons:**

- Does not correct a leaking seam, damaged gutter, or obstructed underground drain.
- Does not remove the need to inspect the system.
- Debris can collect on the guard surface and require attention.

**Best for:** Homeowners seeking a longer-term approach to recurring debris entry after necessary cleaning and repairs.

Ask how the installation affects future access to the gutter. Also request the maintenance instructions before choosing the system; warranty language and maintenance obligations belong in the same decision.

**Verdict: Buy after the gutter system is assessed; wait if the cause of overflow remains unresolved.**

## Match the symptom to the service

Use 3 symptom checks before requesting a proposal. Observe from the ground; do not climb a ladder during rain to diagnose an overflow.

### Debris buildup

Visible leaves and accumulated material point toward a cleaning assessment. Ask the contractor to distinguish loose surface debris from a blocked outlet or downspout.

### Joint leaks

Water escaping at a joint calls for an assessment of that joint. Cleaning can expose the area, but debris removal alone does not repair a failed connection.

### Persistent overflow

Overflow that continues after cleaning needs further investigation. The contractor should assess the water path, gutter alignment, outlet, and downspout rather than immediately recommending another cleaning.


![Three gutter symptoms: debris buildup, joint leaks, and persistent overflow](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/2a84fdd6-3984-4efb-9ffa-3b1572ea9f19/body-28471aedcd6b09bb72f584fa63f70f6c.jpg)

*Describe the symptom before choosing cleaning, repair, or protection.*


A useful service recommendation connects an observed defect to a proposed action. If that connection is missing, ask for an explanation before approving the work.

## Compare proposals without comparing different jobs

Request 2 written proposals using the same scope when you want a meaningful comparison. A short description such as gutter service does not tell you whether the contractor includes downspouts, disposal, inspection, or repairs.

Use this checklist for your 2026 booking:

- **Work area:** Identify which gutters, roof sections, and downspouts are included.
- **Debris removal:** Specify removal from the gutter channel and how collected material will be handled.
- **Downspout assessment:** Ask how the contractor identifies and addresses a blockage.
- **Condition findings:** Request an explanation of leaks, loose sections, or other observed defects.
- **Repair authorization:** Require approval before work outside the agreed scope begins.
- **Completion evidence:** Ask what photos or explanation you will receive afterward.
- **Warranty terms:** Separate any cleaning or repair commitments from a gutter-guard warranty.

Keep 1 written scope with the final agreement. That document should make it possible to answer a simple question after the visit: was the agreed work completed?

If a proposal bundles cleaning, repairs, and guards, ask for each task to be identified separately. You do not need to reject a combined job; you need to understand it.

## Gutter guards versus repeated cleaning

The useful comparison is prevention versus removal—not guards versus never maintaining gutters again. An uncovered gutter admits debris; a guard changes what reaches the channel and where material collects.

For a 2026 decision, judge a guard proposal by the condition of the existing system and the maintenance you will still need to perform. Do not accept maintenance-free language as a replacement for specific instructions.

Ask these questions before approving installation:

- What existing gutter defects need attention first?
- How will the guard attach to the current gutter and roof edge?
- What happens when debris accumulates on the surface?
- How can the gutter be accessed for future service?
- What exactly does the written warranty cover?

For a standalone cleaning, ask the corresponding question: what finding would justify repair or protection instead of repeating the same service? The answer should refer to your home, not a sales script.

## How this shortlist is ranked

The ranking prioritizes service fit, scope clarity, drainage assessment, repair capability, and prevention options. It does not assign review scores, claim firsthand testing, or declare a citywide winner based on unverified comparisons.

The combined-service provider appears first because it offers cleaning, repair, and micro-mesh protection. Standalone cleaning remains the default for a straightforward debris-removal job; guards belong in a separate prevention decision.

## Which gutter service should you choose?

**Choose cleaning for debris, repair for defects, and protection for recurring debris entry.** That rule is more useful than choosing the same package for every house.

For an Eastern Pennsylvania home with overlapping needs, start by asking CleanGutters Lighting to confirm address coverage and define the work. For a cleaning-only problem, compare a focused cleaning scope before considering additional services.

## FAQ


**What's the best way to compare gutter cleaning companies in Philadelphia?**

Compare written scopes for the same work. Confirm gutter clearing, downspout assessment, debris disposal, access arrangements, and how additional repairs require approval.

**Does CleanGutters Lighting serve the Philadelphia area?**

CleanGutters Lighting lists Eastern Pennsylvania within its service area. Confirm coverage for your exact Philadelphia address before scheduling.

**Should I book gutter cleaning or gutter repair?**

Book cleaning for debris removal and request a repair assessment for leaks, loose sections, or other defects. Cleaning alone does not repair a damaged gutter system.

**Do micro-mesh gutter guards eliminate gutter cleaning?**

Micro-mesh gutter guards do not eliminate inspection or maintenance. They limit debris entry, but material can collect on the surface and the drainage system still needs attention.

**Should gutter cleaning include downspouts?**

Your written scope should explicitly state whether downspout assessment and clearing are included. Do not assume a gutter-cleaning description covers every blockage or connected drainage component.

**What should I ask about a transferable lifetime warranty?**

Ask what the warranty covers, what it excludes, and how transfer works. Read maintenance requirements and claim procedures before treating the warranty as a reason to choose an installation.

**What if my gutters still overflow after cleaning?**

Request an assessment of the remaining drainage problem. The contractor should investigate the gutter, outlet, downspout, and relevant connections rather than assuming another cleaning will solve it.


## One last thing

A clean-looking gutter is not proof of a clear drainage path. Water still has to reach the outlet, travel through the downspout, and discharge away from the building.

**Before the contractor leaves, ask what was cleared, what was checked, and what remains unresolved.** That final explanation gives you more useful information than a general claim that the gutters are done.
